articles.title: Microsoft shakes up communications team; CEO Satya Nadella and President Brad Smith sends memo to employees, says 'We will likely have more employees and executives acting as ...'
articles.summary: Microsoft is changing how it communicates with the outside world.
articles.body: Microsoft is changing how it communicates with the outside world. The company is moving its communications team out of its marketing organisation and into the corporate, external and legal affairs group led by Vice Chair and President Brad Smith, according to internal memos from Smith and CEO Satya Nadella. The bigger change, however, may be how Microsoft employees speak for the company. Nadella said the company wants engineers, sellers, partners and other employees who are close to its products and customers to play a bigger role in telling Microsoft's story.“We will likely have more employees and executives acting as part of Microsoft’s public voice, including on social media,” Smith wrote in his memo.Why is Microsoft changing its communications strategyMicrosoft CEO Satya Nadella described the communications shake-up as a response to a media environment that has become “increasingly fragmented and noisier than ever.” Instead of relying mainly on a central communications team to shape Microsoft's public messaging, the CEO wants people closer to the company's work to have a greater role.“In many ways, the people closest to the work have the best opportunity to shape how Microsoft is understood,” Nadella wrote. He said Microsoft wants engineers, sellers, partners and others “closest to our products and customers” to become “an even bigger part of how we tell our story, all connected by a shared strategy and set of principles.”Nadella added: “We will learn, we will experiment, and we will evolve. There is a fundamentally new way to think about communications, and this team will be central to building it.”Microsoft communications team will now report to Brad SmithUnder the new structure, Microsoft's communications function will sit within the organisation led by President Brad Smith rather than under marketing. Smith's organisation handles Microsoft's legal, regulatory and public policy work, including antitrust matters, litigation and government relations.The communications team will therefore sit alongside these functions, although Microsoft plans to continue coordination between communications and marketing.Satya Nadella described Smith as one of the few Microsoft leaders who “embody Microsoft’s voice” authentically. He also praised Smith's “rare ability to communicate complex ideas with clarity, conviction, and trust.”What happens to Microsoft communications chief Frank ShawThe restructuring also changes the role of longtime Microsoft communications chief Frank X. Shaw. Shaw announced earlier this month that he would leave Microsoft at the end of the year after more than two decades with the company. He will now step away from his current responsibilities and serve as an adviser to Smith and interim communications leader Brent Colburn during the transition.Microsoft said Shaw will remain with the company through the end of the year. Shaw described the latest development as the formalisation of the plan that had already been announced.Microsoft said Shaw “has been a trusted counselor and leader at Microsoft for more than two decades, and we’re grateful he will continue to act as an advisor during the transition.”Satya Nadella also thanked Shaw for his contribution. He said Shaw has “made tremendous contributions to the company and to our communications function over the last 17+ years” and has been “a great source of counsel to our leadership team and to me personally, across the company’s biggest moments.”Smith also praised Shaw, saying he had “worked as closely with him as almost anyone” over the years. Smith added that Shaw's “enduring impact on Microsoft and this team will be felt for years to come. I will miss him.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 1991, Greg Norman paid $4.9 million for an 8.3-acre Jupiter Island estate; after rebuilding much of the compound, he sold the Florida property 30 years later for $55.1 million
articles.summary: When Greg Norman bought an 8.3-acre estate on Florida’s Jupiter Island in 1991, the property already offered something difficult to find: privacy, direct
articles.body: When Greg Norman bought an 8.3-acre estate on Florida’s Jupiter Island in 1991, the property already offered something difficult to find: privacy, direct access to the Atlantic Ocean and the Intracoastal Waterway, and enough space for boats, guests and family life. Over the next three decades, however, the golf champion and his wife, Kirsten “Kiki” Norman, transformed the estate into a sprawling compound known as Tranquility. They rebuilt several of its key structures and extensively renovated the rest. According to reports from the Los Angeles Times, Coldwell Banker Global Luxury and Yahoo Sports, the property was eventually sold for about $55.1 million in 2021, which was far above Norman’s original $4.9 million purchase price. The sale marked the end of a long, highly personal real-estate project.Finding Tranquility in 1991Greg Norman was already a major name in professional golf when he purchased the Jupiter Island property. The Australian golfer had become one of the sport’s most recognisable figures, known for his powerful game, distinctive white clothing and nickname, “The Great White Shark.”By 1991, he had also spent years travelling internationally for tournaments. A private waterfront property offered more than luxury. It provided a place to retreat from public life, store boats, entertain friends and create a home base in Florida.The estate stood on approximately 8.3 acres and stretched from the Atlantic Ocean to the Intracoastal Waterway. That unusual layout gave the property water frontage on both sides. The Los Angeles Times reported that the estate had about 370 feet of Intracoastal frontage and 172 feet along the ocean.Norman paid $4.9 million for the property. At the time, it was already one of the original ocean-to-Intracoastal estates on Jupiter Island. Its combination of privacy, water access and scale made it valuable, but Norman and his wife eventually saw the potential to make it more closely reflect their lifestyle.A compound rather than a single houseTranquility was not simply a large mansion. It was a collection of buildings spread across the estate, each serving a different purpose.The compound included a main house, coach house, pool house, tennis house, boat house, carriage house, beach house and orchid house. Together, the buildings contained nearly 32,000 square feet of living and recreational space, according to the Los Angeles Times and Coldwell Banker Global Luxury.This arrangement allowed the property to function almost like a private resort. Guests could stay in separate residences, while family members could enjoy their own spaces. Recreation, fitness, boating, entertaining and relaxation could all happen without leaving the estate.The design also took advantage of the property’s unusual geography. The main residence sat closer to the Intracoastal side, while the beach house faced the Atlantic. Residents could move between calm inland water and open ocean, giving the property two very different coastal experiences.For Norman, the estate also connected with his Australian background and love of boating. It was not designed as a formal showplace alone. It was intended to be used.Rebuilding the visionNorman and Kiki did not merely redecorate the existing property. They rebuilt several of its most important structures.Coldwell Banker Global Luxury reported that the couple completely rebuilt the main house, pool house and beach house, while extensively renovating the other areas of the estate.The rebuilding process allowed them to create a more cohesive compound. The main house was opened up to bring in more natural light and improve views of the coast. Large expanses of glass connected indoor spaces with the water and tropical landscape.Kiki Norman, a hospitality design expert and founder of Norman Design Group, played a central role in shaping the property. Her design approach combined comfort and luxury instead of making the compound feel overly formal.She described the desired atmosphere as “barefoot elegance”, a place that could accommodate high-end entertaining while still feeling relaxed. The goal was to create a sanctuary and a permanent holiday setting for friends and family.That philosophy influenced the choice of materials, colours and layouts. The interiors drew inspiration from the couple’s travels, classic American style and the work of French architect Christian Liaigre.What the estate offeredThe scale of Tranquility was reflected in its amenities.The main house included two wine cellars, each capable of holding about 1,900 bottles. It also contained a movie theatre, trophy room, gallery, wraparound bar and elevator. Walls of glass opened the living areas towards the water views.The pool area included two pools: a 14-foot pool with a diving board and a smaller plunge pool with a spa. The pool house added covered and open terraces, creating spaces for relaxing outdoors throughout the year.A large carriage house provided additional bedrooms along with a gym, cardio room and equipment room. The tennis house was positioned beside a full-size court surrounded by hedges and included a bar and several entertaining areas.The boathouse reflected Norman’s interest in life on the water. The Intracoastal dock could accommodate a yacht of up to 150 feet, according to Coldwell Banker Global Luxury.There was also a generator house with a dog kennel, a detail that revealed how carefully the compound had been designed for practical everyday living rather than appearances alone.A property shaped by waterWater was the defining feature of Tranquility.Many luxury homes offer either ocean frontage or access to a protected waterway. Norman’s estate provided both. The Atlantic side brought wide coastal views, sea breezes and direct beach access. The Intracoastal side offered calmer waters and a substantial dock.That dual orientation influenced both the architecture and the lifestyle of the property. The beach house could serve as a separate oceanfront retreat, while the main house and other structures looked towards the quieter Intracoastal setting.The property also benefited from a nature preserve across the waterway, contributing to its privacy and leafy surroundings. Rather than facing a dense wall of neighbouring construction, parts of the estate looked across at protected natural space.The combination was rare even within an exclusive area such as Jupiter Island. It gave the compound the feeling of a private coastal village, with each building connected to the wider landscape.Listing the estate for saleNorman first placed the estate on the market in 2008, asking $65 million. The property was later relisted and had its price reduced before being withdrawn from the market, according to the Los Angeles Times.The decision to remove the property from sale allowed the Normans to pursue a different strategy. Rather than continuing to market an older compound, they undertook a major rebuilding and renovation project.After the transformation, the estate returned to the market in 2021 with an asking price of $59.9 million. The new listing presented Tranquility as a complete, carefully designed compound rather than simply a large waterfront residence.The relaunch also reflected the work invested in the property. The rebuilt homes, updated amenities, improved interiors and extensive grounds created a finished estate designed for buyers seeking privacy and space.The listing came at a time when luxury buyers were increasingly interested in private properties that could accommodate family, guests, recreation and remote living in one location.The $55.1 million saleThe property did not sell at its full $59.9 million asking price, but it still achieved a remarkable result. Yahoo Sports reported that the estate sold for approximately $55.1 million, with the sale recorded at about $55.095 million.The transaction was completed in April 2021. Reports identified members of the Wexner family, including L Brands chairman emeritus Les Wexner, as the buyers.Compared with Norman’s original $4.9 million purchase price, the sale represented a dramatic increase in value. However, the difference cannot be understood simply as a passive rise in property prices. The estate had been extensively rebuilt, renovated and expanded over three decades.The final price reflected not only its location but also the investment in architecture, landscaping, amenities, privacy and construction. Norman and Kiki had effectively turned an existing waterfront estate into a highly customised compound.The sale also ended a 30-year chapter in the property’s history. What began as a private purchase by a celebrated golfer had become one of the most distinctive luxury estates on Florida’s coast.Life after Jupiter IslandThe Normans continued to own property in Florida after selling Tranquility. Yahoo Sports reported that they purchased a residence in the Old Palm Golf Club community in Palm Beach Gardens for approximately $12.2 million shortly after the Jupiter Island sale.The new home was smaller than Tranquility but still included extensive amenities, including a tennis court, guest house and resort-style pool.The move suggested that the sale was not an exit from Florida but a change in scale and lifestyle. After decades of maintaining a large waterfront compound, a more compact home may have offered privacy and luxury with less responsibility.Norman’s real-estate decisions also took place alongside his continuing business interests. After his golf career, he developed brands connected with golf, wine, clothing and food, while remaining involved in golf-course design and entrepreneurship.More than a luxury saleThe sale of Tranquility is striking because of its numbers: a $4.9 million purchase, an 8.3-acre site, nearly 32,000 square feet of buildings and a final sale price of about $55.1 million.But the property’s story is also about design and personal identity. Norman did not buy a finished mansion and simply occupy it. He reshaped the estate over many years, working with Kiki Norman to create a place that reflected boating, travel, hospitality and outdoor living.The result was a property built around experiences rather than just rooms. Guests could arrive by boat, relax beside the water, play tennis, watch a film, enjoy a meal outdoors or walk from the main compound to the beach.That is what made Tranquility different from an ordinary celebrity home. It was designed as a complete environment—a private coastal retreat that combined privacy with the scale of a resort.After three decades, the estate passed to a new owner at a price more than 11 times Norman’s original purchase figure. Yet the financial gain tells only part of the story. The larger achievement was the transformation of a 1991 purchase into a deeply personal, fully realised Florida compound.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

She liked another post saying Tel Aviv shouldn't exist. You refuse to condemn any of that. You falsely and repeatedly accuse Israel of genocide. Mr. Mamdani, you try to stop me from coming here," Netanyahu said."You tried to silence me. Well, you can't silence me. You can't silence the truth. And here's the simple truth. Here's a simple truth: Israel didn't commit genocide; Israel prevented genocide," he added.Mamdani, the first Muslim mayor of New York, has been a staunch critic of Netanyahu and Israel's military actions in Gaza. He has, on multiple occasions, called the Israeli PM a "war criminal" who is "the architect of a horrific genocide against the Palestinian people."He has also said that his criticism of Israel and advocacy for Palestinian rights do not amount to antisemitism.During his mayoral campaign last year, Mamdani said he would direct police in New York to execute the war crimes court's arrest warrant against Netanyahu, but has more recently acknowledged that the city does not have the authority to take him into custody.The mayor has since encouraged the federal government to arrest Netanyahu, though Trump has said the prime minister will not be arrested.Earlier this week, Mamdani met with US President Donald Trump and repeated his criticism of Israel's actions in Gaza.“As he has done time and again, Prime Minister Netanyahu used his speech to repeat baseless lies meant to sanitise his genocide of Palestinians. articles.title: “Cheap ghee may not be fake” Baba Ramdev explains why good quality ghee can also come at a lower price range
articles.summary: Yoga guru Baba Ramdev recently explained why cow ghee can be sold cheaper too, saying the price is linked to the way the company uses the milk left after
articles.body: Yoga guru Baba Ramdev recently explained why cow ghee can be sold cheaper too, saying the price is linked to the way the company uses the milk left after extracting butter and turns it into other dairy products. Speaking at a press conference in New Delhi on September 23, Ramdev rejected allegations that his brand's cow ghee is fake or adulterated. He said people were drawing conclusions based on hearsay and videos circulating elsewhere. “99% of people are making videos rapidly based only on hearsay,” Ramdev said.How does Ramdev explain the Rs 700 per litre price?Ramdev's explanation focused on the use of milk and its by-products. He said India is the world's largest milk producer and claimed that out of around 100 crore metric tonnes of milk produced globally, around 25 crore metric tonnes comes from India. According to Ramdev, after butter is extracted from milk, the remaining milk does not simply go to waste. He said it can be used to make products such as toned milk, curd, buttermilk, paneer and milk powder.“After we extract butter from the milk, the remaining milk is sold as toned milk. Our cow milk is available in the market at around Rs 50 to Rs 60, which is cheaper than many brands,” he said. He added that the milk can then be used to make several other dairy products. “From that milk, we make curd, buttermilk, paneer or powder. Around 80% of the value of the milk is recovered through these products,” Ramdev said.This, according to his explanation, is an important part of how Patanjali is able to sell its cow ghee at around Rs 700 per litre. “And when ghee is made in a very organised way through this process, this is how ghee is made not only in India but across the world. The toned milk left after making ghee can be converted into powder, curd, buttermilk or paneer,” he said. “It is because of these by-products that we are able to make cow ghee available at around Rs 700 per litre.” Ramdev said this recovery through multiple products allows the company to keep the price of its ghee lower.You use AI every day. articles.title: China's panda diplomacy: How Beijing uses exclusive animal to reinforce soft power
articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping, currently on his state visit in US, announced at the White House that China will send two giant pandas to the United States,
articles.body: Chinese President Xi Jinping, currently on his state visit in US, announced at the White House that China will send two giant pandas to the United States, telling his counterpart Donald Trump: "Here, I have a piece of good news. In a few days, two pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, will come to their new home in Zoo Atlanta and meet with the American people."Xi added that the giant panda has "always been an envoy of friendship between the Chinese and Americans", a language that echoes decades of Chinese messaging around the animals.The names carry their own symbolism: according to Chinese media reports, Fu Shuang translates to "double blessing," while Ping Ping means "peace, peace."That the announcement came directly from Xi, in front of cameras at the White House, rather than through a foreign ministry statement, reflecting how much weight Beijing continues to place on the gesture.The pair's arrival, expected within days, will make Zoo Atlanta the only US zoo housing giant pandas. A milestone in a program that has for more than fifty years doubled as one of Beijing's most effective and most closely watched instruments of soft power.A Cold War icon rebornThe practice traces back to 1972, when Beijing gifted two giant pandas to the United States following President Richard Nixon's historic visit, a gesture that has long served to enhance the country's soft power, with the animals lent to zoos around the world as goodwill ambassadors, and each new transfer often read as a signal of Beijing's approval of stabilised ties with Washington.Since the 1990s, the program evolved from outright gifts into structured, fee-based loans tied explicitly to conservation research. This shift gave Beijing continued leverage while framing the arrangement as scientific cooperation rather than pure political theater.Pandas as a political barometerThe comings and goings of China's pandas have increasingly tracked the temperature of its bilateral relationships. A February 2024 agreement between the San Diego Zoo and China's Wildlife Conservation Association, paving the way for pandas to return to the US, was widely read as more than a zoo transaction as it signaled a warming in US-China relations and an attempt by Beijing to shore up its struggling economy.That reading was reinforced by contrast after China's 2023 withdrawal of its pandas from Washington's Smithsonian Zoo had symbolized just how strained the relationship had become.Atlanta's zoo holds particular significance in that story. It became the only US zoo with pandas after Washington's three bears were flown back to Chengdu aboard a cargo jet under police escort, departing at a moment of strained US-China relations. Ping Ping and Fu Shuang's arrival there, under a 10-year agreement, effectively reopens a channel that had been narrowing for years — and doing so via a leader-to-leader announcement gives it added diplomatic heft.The soft-power calculationPandas are seen not merely as cute animals but as embodiments of a kind of diplomatic tool that China sends abroad, using the gesture to enhance its global image, ease difficult negotiations, and signal friendship or alliance. However, Beijing loans these as gifts to channel significant revenue back into conservation of the panda's native habitat.As of mid-2026, that strategy remains firmly in place. Panda diplomacy continues to function as a cornerstone of China's international soft-power strategy, balancing conservation with geopolitical signaling, even as loan agreements shift toward younger, domestically bred pandas and new breeding partnerships are negotiated with Europe and Southeast Asia.A double-edged swordWhile panda diplomacy remains an effective soft-power tool for Beijing, it also exposes China to public backlash whenever the animals become entangled in political disputes or welfare controversies.That tension surfaced starkly in Japan when the twin pandas Xiao Xiao and Lei Lei were returned to China on January 27. After that Japan was left without a single giant panda for the first time since Tokyo and Beijing normalised relations in 1972.Even so, the animals' pull was undeniable in their final days abroad as roughly 178,000 visitors flocked to Tokyo's Ueno Zoo in the month after the pandas' return was announced, forcing the zoo to cap daily viewing to 4,800 people with one-minute visits.Beijing's careful, tightly managed generosity with a handful of bears, on strict loan terms, deployed at politically opportune moments ensures pandas remain both a diplomatic asset and, occasionally, a domestic and international liability, as debates over animal welfare and nationalist sentiment continue to shadow the program.You use AI every day. articles.title: Why Trump gave Xi a bald eagle sculpture at White House dinner
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump presented Chinese President Xi Jinping with a sculpture of a bald eagle, the national symbol of the United States, during a
articles.body: US President Donald Trump presented Chinese President Xi Jinping with a sculpture of a bald eagle, the national symbol of the United States, during a state dinner at the White House in Washington.The gift was unveiled before VIP guests at Thursday’s dinner and represented “the free and soaring spirit of America”, Trump said.Trump said he and First Lady Melania Trump had participated in the design of the sculpture. The statue is part of the tradition of diplomatic gift-giving, an important but sometimes sensitive aspect of international diplomacy.On Thursday, Xi announced that China would gift two pandas to a zoo in Atlanta and launch a new student exchange programme aimed at welcoming 100,000 US students to study in China over five years."The giant panda have been an envoy of friendship between the Chinese and the Americans," Xi said. "In a few days, two pandas - Ping Ping and Fu Shuang - will come to their new home in Zoo Atlanta and meet with the American people."Gifts have featured prominently during Trump’s presidency, with the US president receiving items including a luxury jumbo jet, an engraved gold bar and a diamond-and-jewel-encrusted gold ring.The US Constitution’s emoluments clause sets a monetary limit on gifts a president can accept from a foreign government. The current limit is $525 (£397). Gifts exceeding that value become federal property unless the president chooses to purchase them with his own money.US presidents are also required to seek congressional approval when accepting certain gifts above the permitted threshold, unless they personally pay for them.Xi is expected to leave Washington after visiting the National Archives, where the Declaration of Independence, the US Constitution and the Bill of Rights are held. The two leaders have sought to maintain ties between the world’s two largest economies, though the visit did not produce major breakthroughs on issues including trade and artificial intelligence safety.The visit comes as the US marks the 250th anniversary of its founding. articles.title: Trump orders steam catapults, but US Navy keeps EMALS alive: Why the switch is difficult
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has ordered the US Navy to return to the old steam catapult for its future Ford-class aircraft carriers.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has ordered the US Navy to return to the old steam catapult for its future Ford-class aircraft carriers. But even as the administration pushes to revive the decades-old technology, the Navy appears to be continuing work on the electromagnetic launch system designed to power its newest carriers.According to Defense News, the Navy has recently awarded contracts related to the Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System, or EMALS, including a $49.3 million contract to Kato Engineering for its energy storage subsystem. The Navy has also sought vendors for additional EMALS components, including recirculation pumps.The development comes after Trump ordered the Navy to prepare a plan to replace EMALS with traditional steam catapults on USS Doris Miller (CVN-81), the next Ford-class aircraft carrier under construction.In an August memo, Trump cited shipbuilding setbacks, cost growth and delays linked to what he described as overly complex designs and repeated design changes. The order also calls for the Ford-class carrier’s electromagnetic weapons elevators to be replaced with hydraulic systems.Why going back to steam is difficult for the NavyThe Ford-class was designed around electromagnetic launch technology, so bringing back steam would require changes to the carrier’s existing design and infrastructure.The problem is even bigger for USS Doris Miller, where nearly 50 percent of production was already complete when the change was ordered. General Atomics has warned that such a switch could add cost, delays and integration risks.The Navy also no longer has the same steam-catapult production base. The service has not ordered a new steam catapult in about two decades, with the last one ordered for USS George H.W. Bush, the final Nimitz-class carrier.The US Navy would have to rebuild the supplier network, manufacturing capacity and technical expertise needed to produce and maintain steam catapults.The Navy says EMALS provides smoother acceleration, more precise launch-speed control, lower maintenance and manpower requirements and the ability to launch aircraft across a wider weight range, including lightweight unmanned aircraft and heavy fighters.Returning to steam would therefore mean not only changing the hardware but also giving up some of the capabilities that the Ford class was designed to provide.The issue is also important for the future of carrier aviation. As the Navy adds more unmanned aircraft to its carrier air wings, it needs a launch system that can handle aircraft of different weights.According to the US Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), EMALS is designed to launch a wide range of aircraft, from lightweight unmanned systems to heavy fighter jets.China is also betting on electromagnetic catapultsChina has also adopted electromagnetic catapult technology for its latest aircraft carrier, the Fujian. The carrier is equipped with three electromagnetic catapults, making it the first Chinese carrier to use the technology.China is taking electromagnetic catapult technology beyond its conventional aircraft carriers, with its Type 076 amphibious assault ship, or LHD, Sichuan, also equipped with an electromagnetic catapult and arresting gear.The move highlights how EMALS is becoming increasingly important not just for traditional carrier operations, but also for the next generation of drone and fixed-wing aircraft platforms.

articles.title: In 1995, Selena’s family made an agreement over profits from her entertainment legacy; 31 years later, brother A.B. Quintanilla is suing sister Suzette for more than $1 million he says he is owed
articles.summary: More than three decades after Selena Quintanilla’s death, a dispute over the business built around her music and legacy has moved into court.
articles.body: More than three decades after Selena Quintanilla’s death, a dispute over the business built around her music and legacy has moved into court. According to court documents obtained by ABC13, Selena’s brother Abraham “A.B.” Quintanilla III has sued his sister, Suzette Quintanilla Arriaga, along with two companies connected to the family’s entertainment business. Filed in Nueces County, Texas, the lawsuit alleges that a family agreement made after Selena’s 1995 death entitled A.B. to 25% of profits from certain entertainment properties. He is seeking more than $1 million, along with an accounting of the estate’s finances.The agreement dates back to 1995Selena was killed in March 1995 at the age of 23. In the months following her death, members of her family entered into what the lawsuit describes as the “Estate Properties Agreement”. According to the court documents, the agreement involved A.B., Suzette, their mother Marcella Quintanilla and Selena’s husband, Christopher Pérez. A.B. says the agreement made him a party to the arrangement and an intended beneficiary.The lawsuit states that he was entitled to receive 25% of the net profits generated by certain entertainment properties connected with Selena. Those interests include aspects of her name, image, likeness, voice, commercial ventures and broader intellectual property. Her music, image and name have continued to generate commercial activity decades after her death.The companies managing Selena’s legacyA key part of the dispute involves two companies named in the lawsuit: Q Production, Inc. and Q Productions, Inc. The court filing says Q Production, Inc. was established by Selena’s father, Abraham Quintanilla Jr., after her death to handle aspects of her entertainment affairs. Suzette later created Q Productions, Inc. in 2025. According to the lawsuit, the newer company became a principal entity through which Selena’s entertainment affairs, intellectual-property rights, commercial ventures and legacy were managed.A.B. alleges that Suzette eventually exercised control over the business activities covered by the family agreement. His lawsuit claims that this resulted in him not receiving the full share of profits to which he believes he was contractually entitled.When A.B. says he discovered the problemThe lawsuit places particular emphasis on 2025. A.B. says he discovered in spring 2025 that he had not received all of the money he believed he was owed. He then sought financial information that would allow him to determine how much had been generated and how much of that amount should have been paid to him.According to the filing, he requested access to financial records but says the information was not provided. The dispute therefore involves more than the amount A.B. is seeking. His lawsuit also asks for a detailed accounting covering Selena’s estate and related business activity. The filing seeks records dating from 2016 through the present, as well as more than $1 million in unpaid profits and proceeds. A.B. is also seeking attorney fees and court costs.Suzette and Marcella dispute the allegationsThe allegations have been disputed by Suzette and their mother, Marcella Quintanilla. In a joint statement posted on Selena’s official social media account before the lawsuit was formally filed, the two rejected suggestions that Suzette had stolen or improperly taken money or property belonging to A.B., other family members, Selena’s estate or jointly owned family businesses. They also questioned A.B.’s earlier public references to a lawsuit and alleged wrongdoing involving their late father. At the time of that statement, they said they had not found a publicly filed case matching the description A.B. had given.The subsequent court filing in Nueces County has now established that A.B. has filed a civil lawsuit naming Suzette and the two companies. The family’s earlier response nonetheless remains relevant to the dispute because it shows that the allegations were contested before the case became public through the court documents.Selena’s legacy remains a family businessThe dispute comes against the backdrop of a legacy that has grown considerably since Selena’s death. During her lifetime, Selena performed with Selena y Los Dinos, the family band in which both A.B. and Suzette also played. A.B. became an important songwriter and producer for the group, while Suzette played drums before later becoming involved in the business surrounding her sister’s legacy.After Selena’s death, her music and image continued to be used across recordings, merchandise, licensing, entertainment projects and other commercial ventures. Managing her estate and intellectual property has remained central to the family’s business activities. Her father, Abraham Quintanilla Jr., who had played a central role in managing Selena’s career, died in December 2025 at age 86. The lawsuit now raises questions about the financial arrangements governing the estate after his death.What A.B. is asking the court to decideThe lawsuit does not simply seek a payment. A.B. is asking for financial records that would establish how much money was generated from the relevant entertainment properties and determine what portion he believes he is entitled to receive under the 1995 agreement. articles.summary: A NEWDERY power bank sold online for as little as $27 has been recalled in the US after nine reports of the devices exploding and catching fire, according
articles.body: A NEWDERY power bank sold online for as little as $27 has been recalled in the US after nine reports of the devices exploding and catching fire, according to the US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). One of the incidents involved a serious fire that caused an estimated $2 million in property damage, while another resulted in a burn injury. The recall, announced on September 24, 2026, affects about 21,380 power banks with model number ZHX-PB22. The lithium-ion batteries inside the devices can explode or ignite, creating fire and burn hazards. The affected products were sold on Amazon.com between October 2023 and November 2024 for between $27 and $50.Which power banks are being recalled after nine reports of units explodingThe recall covers NEWDERY power banks with the model number ZHX-PB22. The affected units are black and come with yellow cables. The NEWDERY brand name is engraved on the front, while the model number is printed on the back of the device. The products were manufactured in China and imported by Shenzhen Xinkewangda Electronics Co., Ltd., doing business as NEWDERY. According to the CPSC, about 21,380 units are covered by the September 2026 recall. The recalled power bank is a portable device containing a lithium-ion battery. The CPSC says the battery can explode or ignite, presenting fire and burn hazards to consumers. Consumers who have one of the affected devices can check the model number on the back of the power bank. They should not rely only on the appearance of the device, as the specific model number, ZHX-PB22, is the key identifier given in the recall notice.Nine reports included explosions and firesThe recall follows nine reports received by NEWDERY involving the recalled power banks exploding and igniting.One of those reports involved a serious fire that caused approximately $2 million in property damage, according to the CPSC. Another report involved a burn injury. The CPSC has not provided further details in its recall notice about the location of the $2 million fire, what property was damaged or how the incident unfolded. Those details should therefore not be inferred beyond the agency's description. The agency identifies the lithium-ion battery as the source of the hazard. Lithium-ion batteries can store substantial amounts of energy, and failures can result in overheating, fire or other dangerous events. In this case, the CPSC specifically warns that the battery in the recalled NEWDERY power banks can explode or ignite.The power banks were sold on Amazon for $27 to $50The affected power banks were sold through Amazon.com from October 2023 to November 2024, according to the latest CPSC recall notice. Their reported selling price ranged from $27 to $50. That means the $27 figure refers to the lowest reported selling price for the recalled product, rather than the price of the particular power bank involved in the $2 million property-damage incident. The September 2026 recall covers about 21,380 units. The products were manufactured in China and imported by Shenzhen Xinkewangda Electronics Co., Ltd., which operates under the NEWDERY name. There is also an important history behind the recall. In June 2025, the CPSC had already warned consumers to immediately stop using NEWDERY ZHX-PB22 power banks after receiving the same nine reports of explosions and fires. At that time, the agency said about 17,670 defective units had been sold exclusively on Amazon from March 2023 through November 2024 for $27 to $50. The 2025 notice said the importer had refused to conduct a recall. The figures from the two notices should not be combined. The 17,670-unit figure belongs to the June 2025 warning, while the 21,380-unit figure belongs to the September 2026 recall.Consumers have been told to stop using the deviceThe CPSC is now telling consumers to stop using the recalled power banks immediately and contact NEWDERY for instructions on obtaining a full refund. Consumers seeking a refund will have to provide a photograph of the recalled power bank showing its model number and serial number, along with the word ‘recalled’ and the consumer's last name written on the device in permanent marker. They will also have to confirm that the power bank has been disposed of in accordance with applicable laws and regulations. The disposal instructions are particularly important because the CPSC says recalled lithium-ion batteries should not be placed in ordinary household rubbish or general recycling.Consumers are also advised not to put the device into street-level or curbside recycling bins or used battery recycling boxes commonly found at retail and home-improvement stores. Instead, they should contact their local household hazardous waste collection centre to ask whether it accepts recalled lithium-ion batteries. If it does not, the CPSC advises consumers to contact their municipality for further guidance.What consumers should check before seeking a refundAnyone who owns a NEWDERY power bank should first check whether it matches the recalled model. The key identifier is ZHX-PB22, printed on the back. The recalled units are black and have yellow cables, with the NEWDERY name on the front. The CPSC lists NEWDERY's consumer contact number as 888-256-6673, available from 11am to 7pm ET Monday through Friday. Consumers can also contact the company by email at support@newdery.com or use the recall information provided on NEWDERY's website. The September 24 recall carries CPSC recall number 26-792. For consumers, the central message is straightforward, if the power bank is the recalled ZHX-PB22 model, it should no longer be used, and it should be handled through the recall and appropriate hazardous-waste disposal process rather than being thrown into ordinary rubbish or recycling.You use AI every day. articles.title: Pumping life into Mecca Pact? Saudi, Turkey, Pakistan plan urgent meet as Houthis step up attacks
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan are preparing for an urgent meeting of their military chiefs after a fresh wave of Houthi attacks on the kingdom, in a
articles.body: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan are preparing for an urgent meeting of their military chiefs after a fresh wave of Houthi attacks on the kingdom, in a move that could put their newly signed defence pact, also called Mecca deal, to its first major test.The talks will be held under the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, which says an armed attack on any one of the three countries will be treated as an attack on all three.The planned meeting was announced after the foreign ministers of the three countries met in New York on Thursday. Saudi foreign minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan, Pakistan's deputy prime minister and foreign minister Ishaq Dar, and Turkish foreign minister Hakan Fidan discussed the attacks and possible steps under the agreement.The Saudi foreign ministry did not give a date for the military chiefs' meeting or specify what form of support Saudi Arabia could receive.Pact under first major testSaudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement on August 7 with the aim of strengthening their collective deterrence and defence cooperation.The three countries have since begun putting the agreement's mechanisms in place. Their foreign and defence ministers and military chiefs met in Istanbul on August 31 for the first meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee. They agreed to establish a secretariat in Saudi Arabia and expand military cooperation.During Thursday's meeting, the three foreign ministers condemned attacks on Mecca and on civilian and economic facilities in Saudi Arabia. They also backed Riyadh's right to defend itself under Article 51 of the UN Charter, which recognises a country's right to self-defence.The ministers also discussed regional stability, freedom of navigation and their commitment to reducing tensions through diplomatic and peaceful means.Saudi Arabia reports fresh missile attacksThe diplomatic push came as Saudi Arabia reported another wave of attacks launched from Yemen. Saudi authorities said their air defences intercepted six ballistic missiles fired towards Taif and Yanbu on Thursday. Major-General Turki al-Malki, spokesman for the coalition, warned that any further Houthi escalation would be “dealt with firmly”.Saudi civil defence authorities had earlier issued alerts in several areas before later saying the threat had passed.The Houthis, meanwhile, claimed to have carried out missile and drone attacks against what they called a “sensitive target” in Riyadh and facilities belonging to Saudi Aramco in Yanbu.France has also offered defensive support to Saudi Arabia. French President Emmanuel Macron said Paris would send military assets to help protect Yanbu.“We are going to send military assets, meaning soldiers, radars and defence systems to protect this site,” Macron said in an interview with TF1 on Thursday.Fighting intensifies inside YemenThe cross-border attacks have come alongside some of the heaviest fighting inside Yemen since the conflict escalated again.At least 150 fighters from the Houthi and government-aligned forces were killed in the 24 hours before Friday, according to news agency AFP. The figure included 98 fighters from the government side and 52 Houthis.Fighting was reported around the Kahboub Mountains and areas between Lahj and Taiz overlooking the Bab al-Mandeb Strait.The Houthis have also expanded their presence along Yemen's Red Sea coast, including around the port city of Mocha and strategic islands. Their gains have strengthened their position near Bab al-Mandeb, a major global shipping route through which about 12% of global trade normally passes, according to AP.Yemen's internationally recognised government has called for greater international involvement. Speaking at the UN General Assembly, Vice President Abdullah Abdulkader Al Alimi-Bawzer warned that Houthi control around the strait could have wider economic consequences.He accused the group of using freedom of navigation as leverage, saying its actions were “taking hostage the entire global economy”.The renewed fighting has also triggered a major displacement crisis. More than 230,000 people have been forced from their homes since the beginning of September, according to UNHCR. The latest displacement adds to an estimated 5.2 million people already internally displaced across Yemen.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
